newsitem.title: INDIA: India call dormant on reporting day, gilts active.
newsitem.headline: India call dormant on reporting day, gilts active.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed easy at 0.10-0.50 percent, down from 0.25-0.75 percent opening, in dull trading on the reporting Friday, dealers said.
Three-day money was traded in the region of 3.0-4.0 percent with some stray deals above 4.0 percent, a dealer said.
"This indicates the opening levels for Saturday at 4.5-5.5 percent," he said. "Call may slide down towards the close on State Bank of India (SBI)'s lending support," he added.
The interbank term money dealt in the region of 7.25-7.75 percent for one-month maturity, a dealer said.
The securities market witnessed some buying interest on lower call levels, a dealer with a foreign bank said.
Short-term paper prices were largely unchanged with the trading interest diverted from medium term to long term paper.
The 12.50 percent government stock 2004 maintained its price rally on Friday, which appreciated by 30 paise to close at 100.65 rupees, dealers said.
The 13.05 percent 2007 stock rose to 102.10 rupees from 101.97 rupees, dealers said.
The newly-auctioned paper 12.59 percent 2004 reported a deal at 100.95 rupees compared to the previous 100.85 rupees.
The state development loans also attracted trading interest with 13.05 percent 2007 stock rising to 101.25 rupees from 100.65 rupees, he added.
Yield on treasury bills maturing in September 1997 fell to 7.00 percent from its previous 7.15 percent, a dealer said.
